meals.name: Greek yoghurt, berries & seeds
steps: Add yoghurt to a bowl.
Top with berries, oats and seeds.
Serve immediately.
meals.fit: A simple option with protein, fibre and calcium.

meals.name: Avocado, egg & seeded toast
steps: Toast the bread.
Cook the eggs to your preference.
Mash avocado over toast and top with egg and spinach.
meals.fit: A balanced breakfast with fibre and healthy fats.

meals.name: Overnight oats with banana & seeds
steps: Mix oats, milk and chia.
Refrigerate overnight.
Top with sliced banana.
meals.fit: An easy make ahead breakfast with useful fibre.

meals.name: Salmon, quinoa & greens
steps: Cook quinoa.
Cook salmon and pepper.
Serve with greens and quinoa.
Finish with olive oil and lemon.
meals.fit: A protein rich lunch with omega 3 and vegetables.

meals.name: Chickpea, cucumber & herb bowl
steps: Rinse chickpeas.
Chop cucumber and tomatoes.
Toss with herbs and olive oil.
meals.fit: A plant forward lunch with plenty of fibre.

meals.name: Chicken, rice & roasted peppers
steps: Cook rice.
Roast peppers and courgette.
Cook chicken thoroughly.
Serve together.
meals.fit: A familiar, high protein meal with colourful vegetables.

meals.name: Lentil & roasted vegetable bowl
steps: Chop vegetables.
Roast until tender.
Warm lentils.
Combine with spinach and vegetables.
meals.fit: A fibre rich plant forward option. For digestive symptoms, individual tolerance to lentils and other high fibre foods varies.

meals.name: Cod, potatoes & green beans
steps: Boil potatoes.
Bake or pan cook cod until fully cooked.
Steam green beans.
Serve with lemon and olive oil.
meals.fit: A lighter fish based dinner with protein and vegetables.

meals.name: Chicken & sweet potato tray bake
steps: Chop vegetables.
Place chicken and vegetables on a tray.
Add oil and seasoning.
Roast until chicken is fully cooked.
meals.fit: A practical tray bake when you want something hearty and simple.

meals.name: Ghanaian grilled tilapia & fries
steps: Blend or finely chop pepper, onion, ginger and garlic, then rub it over the fish.
Leave the fish to take on the flavour for about 20 minutes.
Heat the grill or oven to 180°C and cook the tilapia for about 10 to 15 minutes on each side until the flesh flakes easily.
Cut the yam into chip shapes and cook until golden and tender, or use potato fries if that is what you have.
Serve with pepper sauce, sliced onion and the yam chips.
meals.fit: A Ghanaian favourite built around grilled fish, traditionally paired with yam and hot pepper sauce; this home version can use fries if preferred.

meals.name: Swedish köttbullar with lingonberry
steps: Soften the onion gently for about 5 minutes.
Mix mince, onion, breadcrumbs, egg and milk until just combined.
Roll into small meatballs.
Brown them in a pan, turning often, then cook through for about 10 minutes.
Serve with potatoes, sauce and lingonberry.
meals.fit: A classic Swedish comfort meal, often served with potatoes and lingonberry.

meals.name: True ramen · shoyu style
meals.meta: China to Japan · Wheat noodles · Umami
steps: Bring the broth to a gentle simmer and season with soy sauce.
Cook the noodles according to the packet until springy, usually about 3 to 4 minutes.
Warm mushrooms in the broth for 2 minutes.
Add noodles to a bowl and pour over the hot broth.
Top with egg, spring onion and nori.
meals.fit: Ramen has Chinese roots and became a distinct Japanese food with many regional styles. This is a simple shoyu inspired home bowl.

meals.name: Vietnamese chicken phở
steps: Warm the stock with ginger and star anise for about 15 minutes.
Cook the rice noodles according to the packet, usually 3 to 5 minutes.
Add cooked sliced chicken to the hot broth.
Build the bowl with noodles, broth and herbs.
Finish with lime and chilli to taste.
meals.fit: A fragrant Vietnamese noodle soup with fresh herbs and citrus.

meals.name: Korean bibimbap
steps: Cook the rice and keep it warm.
Cook each vegetable separately for a few minutes so it stays colourful and tender.
Fry the egg until the white is set.
Build the rice bowl with vegetables and egg.
Add gochujang and sesame oil, then mix at the table.
meals.fit: A Korean mixed rice bowl that brings vegetables, rice, sauce and protein together.

meals.name: Fijian kokoda
ingredients: 180g very fresh fish suitable for raw preparation
steps: Cut the fish into small pieces and cover with lime juice.
Chill while the citrus changes the fish texture, following a food safe recipe and using suitable fresh fish.
Mix coconut milk with tomato, cucumber and onion.
Combine with the fish and chilli just before serving.
meals.fit: Kokoda is a Fijian dish of fish prepared with citrus and coconut, often enjoyed as a fresh shared dish.

meals.name: Masala dosa with sambar
meals.meta: South India · Fermented batter · Plant based
steps: Warm the pan and spread a thin layer of dosa batter.
Cook until the underside is crisp and golden, about 2 to 3 minutes.
Fill with spiced potato and fold.
Warm the sambar and serve with coconut chutney.
meals.fit: Dosa is a fermented South Indian staple with many regional styles and accompaniments.

meals.name: Peruvian ceviche
ingredients: 180g very fresh fish suitable for raw preparation
steps: Dice the fish and keep it properly chilled.
Prepare the lime, onion, chilli and coriander.
Combine shortly before serving according to a trusted food safe method.
Serve with sweetcorn and sweet potato.
meals.fit: Peruvian ceviche is a traditional dish closely connected with coastal food culture and communal eating.

meals.name: Amazonian tacacá
steps: Prepare the manioc based broth using a food safe commercial preparation.
Cook jambu until tender.
Make a small tapioca starch portion according to the recipe.
Assemble the hot broth with jambu, tapioca and shrimp.
Serve very hot in a bowl, as traditionally presented.
meals.fit: Tacacá is associated with Indigenous food traditions of northern Brazil and the Amazon region.

meals.name: Hawaiian poke bowl
ingredients: 150g sushi grade or otherwise suitable fish
steps: Keep the fish properly chilled and use fish suitable for raw consumption.
Cut the fish into bite sized pieces.
Toss gently with shoyu, sesame and green onion.
Serve over warm or cooled rice with cucumber and seaweed.
meals.fit: Poke is rooted in Native Hawaiian food culture, with later influences creating many modern variations.

meals.name: Lemon herb salmon, avocado & greens
steps: Pat the salmon dry and season lightly.
Pan cook for about 4 minutes on each side, depending on thickness, until it flakes easily.
Slice the avocado and cucumber while the salmon cooks.
Build the greens, avocado and cucumber, then add the salmon.
Finish with lemon and olive oil.
meals.fit: A low carbohydrate meal built around salmon, avocado and leafy greens. Keto suitability depends on the full recipe and your daily carbohydrate target.

meals.name: Nepali dal bhat tarkari
steps: Warm the lentils with tomato, cumin and turmeric for 5 minutes.
Cook the vegetables until just tender, about 7 minutes.
Warm the rice and spoon everything into a bowl.
Finish with coriander and a little pickle if you like.
meals.fit: A varied meal built around lentils, vegetables and rice.

meals.name: Ghanaian jollof rice with beans
steps: Blend or finely chop the tomato, pepper and onion.
Cook the mixture for 10 minutes until thick and glossy.
Stir in rice and enough water or stock to cook it through.
Fold through beans near the end and rest for 5 minutes.
meals.fit: A flavourful plant forward option with rice, beans and vegetables.

meals.name: Shakshuka with wholegrain bread
steps: Soften onion and pepper for 5 minutes.
Add chopped tomatoes and paprika and simmer for 8 minutes.
Make two wells and crack in the eggs. Cover and cook for 4 to 6 minutes until set to your liking.
Serve with toasted wholegrain bread.
meals.fit: A vegetable rich breakfast with protein and fibre.

meals.name: Japanese salmon rice bowl
steps: Cook the salmon until it flakes easily, about 8 to 10 minutes depending on thickness.
Warm the rice.
Slice cucumber and spring onion.
Build the bowl and finish with edamame and sesame.
meals.fit: A colourful bowl combining fish, grains and vegetables.

meals.name: Moroccan chickpea vegetable tagine
steps: Soften carrot and onion for 5 minutes.
Add spices and stir for 30 seconds.
Add tomatoes, courgette and chickpeas and simmer for 15 minutes.
Finish with coriander and lemon.
meals.fit: A vegetable and legume based meal with aromatic spices.

meals.name: Caribbean black bean & plantain bowl
steps: Slice plantain and cook in a little oil until golden on both sides.
Warm beans with tomato and seasoning.
Shred cabbage and slice avocado.
Build the bowl and finish with lime.
meals.fit: A colourful combination of beans, plantain and fresh vegetables.

meals.name: Ethiopian lentil stew with greens
steps: Cook onion, garlic and berbere gently for 5 minutes.
Add tomatoes and simmer until thick.
Stir in lentils and cook for 8 minutes.
Fold through spinach until wilted and serve.
meals.fit: A fibre rich lentil dish with greens and warming spices.

meals.name: Greek lentil, tomato & feta bowl
steps: Rinse and drain the lentils.
Chop tomato and cucumber.
Toss with parsley and olive oil.
Crumble over feta and serve.
meals.fit: A simple bowl built around lentils, vegetables and a little feta.

meals.name: Mexican black bean, corn & avocado bowl
steps: Warm the beans and corn with a little cumin.
Chop tomatoes and avocado.
Combine everything in a bowl.
Finish with lime and coriander.
meals.fit: A flexible plant forward bowl with beans, vegetables and avocado.

meals.name: Middle Eastern lentil soup with wholegrain flatbread
steps: Soften onion and carrot for 5 minutes.
Add tomatoes, cumin and lentils with enough water to cover.
Simmer for 15 minutes and stir until the soup thickens.
Warm the flatbread and serve alongside.
meals.fit: A simple lentil based meal with vegetables and aromatic spices.

Nepal.description: Dal bhat tarkari brings lentils, rice, vegetables and pickles together in one of Nepal’s most recognisable everyday meals.

Ghana.description: Ghanaian jollof is built around rice, tomato, aromatics and spices, with beans, fish, chicken or vegetables often alongside it.

Mediterranean.description: Across the Mediterranean, vegetables, legumes, grains, herbs, olive oil and fish create many different food traditions rather than one fixed diet.

Morocco.description: Chickpeas, vegetables, herbs and warm spices make Moroccan tagines a wonderful gateway to North African flavours.

Japan.description: Rice, fish, vegetables, fermented foods and simple seasonings create many Japanese everyday meals.

Caribbean.description: Beans, plantain, fish, vegetables, herbs and fruit appear in many colourful Caribbean food traditions.

Middle East.description: Legumes, grains, vegetables, herbs, yoghurt and spices create a huge variety of Middle Eastern dishes.

Ethiopia.description: Lentils, vegetables, greens and aromatic spice blends make Ethiopian food a rich place to explore.

Latin America.description: Beans, maize, avocado, vegetables and herbs form a starting point for countless Latin American dishes.

Sweden.description: Swedish food ranges from everyday comfort dishes to breads, fish, potatoes and seasonal traditions. Köttbullar are one familiar example, often paired with potatoes and lingonberry.

Vietnam.description: Vietnamese cooking is known for aromatic broths, fresh herbs, rice noodles, vegetables, chilli and bright citrus.

Korea.description: Korean food brings together rice, vegetables, fermented foods, sauces and many regional traditions. Bibimbap is a vivid example.

Fiji.description: Fijian food reflects island life, the ocean, tropical produce and a strong tradition of sharing food. Kokoda and lovo offer two very different ways in.

India.description: India contains an extraordinary range of regional cuisines. Dosa is one South Indian example; spices, grains, legumes and fermentation appear in many traditions.

Peru.description: Peruvian cuisine spans coast, Andes and Amazon, with ceviche deeply connected to coastal traditions, local produce and communal occasions.

Amazon.description: Amazonian foodways draw on river fish, manioc, native plants and Indigenous knowledge. Tacacá is a striking example from northern Brazil.

Hawaiʻi.description: Native Hawaiian food traditions include staples such as kalo and poi and a deep relationship with land, sea and community. Modern island food also reflects many later influences.
